sentences.text: The present case has its genesis in an information dated 20.02.2014 lodged before respondent police by the defacto complainant, none other than the wife of appellant No.1.

The said information led to registration of FIR bearing No.109/2014 against the appellants/accused Nos.1 and 2 for offences punishable under Section 498A and 307 r/w 34 of IPC.
3.

On a full-fledged trial, the learned Sessions Judge has found both the accused guilty of the offence punishable under Section 498A r/w 34 of IPC, while acquitting them of the offence punishable under Section 307 r/w 34 of IPC.

4. Learned counsel for the appellants has filed an affidavit signed by both the appellants as well as defacto complainant, impleaded as respondent No.2, NC: 2024:KHC:40708 wherein it is stated that the parties have settled their disputes.
An application is filed to permit the appellants to enter into a settlement with the informant i.e., Smt.Anu Singh daughter of Dr. S.K.Singh and consequently to acquit the appellants.

5. It is stated that during the time of passage of judgment and order dated 04.07.2024, appellant No.1 and the informant who were parties in various capacities before various Courts at New Delhi,
entered into a settlement agreement dated 30.07.2024 before the Delhi High Court Mediation and Conciliation Centre, in the matter bearing M & C File No.165/2024, wherein the parties have decided to end all litigations between themselves and also agreed on certain terms and conditions to extinguish such lis between themselves, including the present matter.
6.

entities.text: Delhi High Court Mediation and Conciliation Centre
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Certified copy of the order dated 09.08.2024 along with the settlement agreement dated 30.07.2024 is produced at Annexure-A.
At NC: 2024:KHC:40708 clause (iv) of the settlement agreement, reference has been made to the present appeal.
7. As per the settlement, a total sum of Rs.80,00,000/- shall be paid by appellant No.1 herein to respondent No.2, in four equal installments.
Towards first installment, the appellants have agreed to pay a sum of Rs.20,00,000/- today and respondent No.2/informant has agreed to receive the said sum.

8. Respondent No.2/defacto complainant who is present before the Court has agreed to the terms of settlement and also submits that she has received a sum of Rs.20,00,000/- towards first installment by way of D.D. bearing No.500991 dated 27.09.2024 drawn on ICICI Bank, Chandini Chowk Branch, Delhi.
9. The appellants as well as respondent No.2 have accepted that they will abide with the settlement agreement dated 30.07.2024, produced at Annexure-A. NC: 2024:KHC:40708 10.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in Ramagopal and another V. State of Madhya Pradesh has held at para No.13 as under:
13.

sentences.text: Handing out punishment is not the sole form of delivering justice.
Societal method of applying laws evenly is always subject to lawful exceptions.

It goes without saying, that the cases where compromise is struck post conviction, the High Court ought to exercise such discretion with rectitude, keeping in-view the circumstances surrounding the incident, the fashion in which the compromise has been arrived at, and with due regard to the nature and seriousness of the offence, besides the conduct of the accused, before 2021 SCC online SC 834 NC:
2024:KHC:40708 and after the incidence.
The touchstone for exercising the extra-ordinary power under Section 482 Cr.P.C. would be to secure the ends of justice.
There can be no hard and fast line constricting the power of the High Court to do substantial justice.

A restrictive construction of inherent powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C. may lead to rigid or specious justice, which in the given facts and circumstances of a case, may rather lead to grave injustice.

On the other hand, in cases where heinous offences have been proved against perpetrators, no such benefit ought to be extended, as cautiously observed by this Court in Narinder Singh v State of Punajab and Laxmi Narayan (Supra).
11.

entities.text: Narinder Singh v State of Punajab and Laxmi Narayan
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In 2JITENDRA RAGHUVANSHI AND OTHERS vs. BABITA RAGHUVANSHI AND ANOTHER,
the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that, the inherent powers of the High Court under Section 482 of Criminal Procedure Code are wide and unfettered.

entities.text: 2JITENDRA RAGHUVANSHI AND OTHERS vs. BABITA RAGHUVANSHI AND ANOTHER
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is the duty of the Courts to 2013(3) Crimes 90 (SC) NC: 2024:KHC:40708 encourage genuine settlements of matrimonial disputes, particularly,
when the same are on considerable increase.

Even if the offences are non- compoundable, if they relate to matrimonial disputes and the Court is satisfied that, the parties have settled the same amicably and without any pressure, for the purpose of securing ends of justice, Section 320 of the Code, would not be a bar to the exercise of power of quashing of FIR.

12. In the case of B.S.JOSHI vs. STATE OF HARYANA, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has upheld the powers of the High Court under Section 482 of the code to quash criminal proceedings, where dispute is of a private nature and a compromise is entered into between the parties who are willing to settle their differences amicably."
13. In the case on hand, the appellants are convicted by the trial Court for the offence punishable under Section 498A r/w 34 of IPC.

The parties have filed an affidavit stating that they have resolved the (2003)4 SCC 675 NC: 2024:KHC:40708 entire dispute, in terms of settlement agreement dated 30.07.2024 before the Delhi High Court Mediation and Conciliation Centre, certified copy of the order dated 09.08.2024 and the settlement agreement which are annexed along with the memo and affidavit.

entities.text: Delhi High Court Mediation and Conciliation Centre
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 14. The offence alleged is predominantly private in nature.
The Hon'ble Apex Court has permitted such compromise to be recorded post conviction by the High Court exercising its jurisdiction under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.

In the light of the decisions noted supra, it is just and proper, in the interest of justice, to exercise the inherent power vested in this Court under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., and to allow the appeal.
